title: Invertibility of the affine tower counit transpose
statement: Let N>0, let A be a finite commutative ring annihilated by N, and let t and D be the normalized ordinary finite Tate transport and projective-line data of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-data]. For every Noetherian scheme S on which N is invertible and every d>=0, the actual counit transpose towerAdjoint of [def-trf-coordinate-counit-arrows] is an isomorphism. This is the transpose under the actual unbounded compact-support/exceptional adjunction of the ordered tower counit, including its specified bounded-to-unbounded compact-support comparison and the single/derived-unit comparison.

source.place: Local construction, affine-space adjunction: invertibility of the ordered counit transpose (parent proof Step 1).

proof.text: At the tower right functor applied to the ordinary constant coefficient, identify affineLinearCompactComparison with the restriction of affineTraceUnboundedCompactComparison using [lem-amb-affine-trace-compact-comparison-restriction]. Cancel the bounded compatibility isomorphism to obtain equality of the comparison homs.

Transport the ordered tower adjunction of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] along the unbounded compact-support comparison. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to it and the canonical exceptional adjunction. Transpose the component of this isomorphism at ordinaryFiniteUnit; the counit formula for rightAdjointUniq identifies it with the defining compact-comparison inverse followed by the tower counit. Naturality in the final single/derived-unit isomorphism proves that towerAdjoint is the isomorphism component followed by the exceptional functor applied to that unit isomorphism. Both factors are invertible. This remains valid for d=0, empty S, and A=0.
